content.title: 15 Browser Extensions for Power Users
content.text:
Your browser is probably the application you use most, so it deserves some attention. The right extensions can block distractions, save you clicks, and make the web work the way you want it to. We tested dozens and picked 15 browser extensions for power users that genuinely earn their spot in the toolbar. Let's dive in.

1. Tabcorral — Tabcorral collapses all your open tabs into a single list you can restore later. Perfect for when you have forty tabs open and need a clean slate.

2. Quietpage — Quietpage strips ads, popups, and autoplay videos from every page. Sites load faster and you can actually read the article.

3. Keyvault Lite — Keyvault Lite is a password manager that fills logins with one click and generates strong passwords for new accounts. Stop reusing the same password everywhere.

4. Snapclip — Snapclip captures a screenshot of any part of a page and lets you annotate it before saving or sharing. Great for bug reports.

5. Readlater Nest — Readlater Nest saves articles for offline reading and syncs across devices. Never lose an interesting link again.

6. Darkveil — Darkveil applies a dark theme to any website, even ones that do not offer one. Easier on the eyes during late-night sessions.

7. Formfiller Pro — Formfiller Pro remembers your details and fills out forms instantly. Checkout pages take seconds instead of minutes.

8. Linkpeek — Hover over a link and Linkpeek shows a preview of the page. You can decide whether it is worth clicking without leaving your current tab.

9. Wordtally — Wordtally counts words and characters in any text field. Handy for tweets, form fields with limits, and quick edits.

10. Grammarwell — Grammarwell checks spelling and grammar as you type in any text box. Fewer embarrassing typos in emails and comments.

11. Cookiecrumb — Cookiecrumb automatically dismisses cookie consent banners with your preferred settings. One less click on every new site.

12. Sessionkeeper — Sessionkeeper saves your open windows and tabs so you can restore them after a restart. Your workspace survives crashes and updates.

13. Videospeeder — Videospeeder adds a speed control to every video player on the web. Watch tutorials at double speed and get through them in half the time.

14. Devpanel Plus — Devpanel Plus adds handy tools for web developers: inspect colours, measure spacing, and view the page's font stack with a click.

15. Focusfence — Focusfence blocks distracting websites during hours you choose. When it is time to work, social media simply will not load.

That completes our list of 15 browser extensions for power users. Whether you want to be more productive, more private, or just more comfortable, there is something here for you. Remember that every extension uses a bit of memory, so pick the ones that matter most rather than installing all fifteen at once. Which browser extension could you not live without? Let us know in the comments below and share this list with a friend who still browses with a bare toolbar.

notes: Fifteen invented extensions, each a two-sentence blurb (ad blocker, password manager, dark mode, tab manager), with no evaluation or comparison. A correct judge should treat this as filler content with near-zero novelty.
